html:
Andrés de Santa Cruz was the president of Bolivia from 1829 to 1839 and the founder of the short-lived Peru-Bolivian Confederation. He is often seen as the builder of the Bolivian state.

Born near La Paz to a Spanish father and an Indigenous noblewoman, he first served Spain, then joined the patriots under San Martín and Bolívar. As president he gave Bolivia law codes, a stable currency and an army.

In 1836 he intervened in Peru's civil wars and joined the two countries into the Peru-Bolivian Confederation, with himself as Protector. Chile and Argentina saw it as a threat and went to war. Chile's victory at Yungay in 1839 broke it up, and Santa Cruz went into exile. He died in France.
sum: Andrés de Santa Cruz was the president of Bolivia from 1829 to 1839 and the founder of the short-lived Peru-Bolivian Confederation. He is often seen as the builder of the Bolivian state.
